## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`test_rejects_legacy_header` should be fixed: it passes because its fixture has no `END` line, not because the version check works. The header change in `app/report.py` is correct, and `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` covers it.

## Changes
`parse_report` now accepts only the exact header `REPORT v1` instead of any header starting with `REPORT `. The pull request also adds two tests that check unsupported headers are rejected.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:10 — tests — Make the legacy-header test reach the version check — `rsplit("v1", 1)` replaces only the last `v1`, so the fixture becomes `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`: the header stays `REPORT v1` and there is no `END` line. `parse_report` returns `None` at the `END` check in `app/report.py:3`, so the test still passes if the header check is removed. The comment at line 9 says it changes "the fixture's version to v0", which the code does not do. — The test gives no regression protection for the header rule it names, and its comment points maintainers to the wrong failure path. — Fix: Use a complete fixture such as `"REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND"`, or remove the test because `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` already covers this input.
